claims.claim: in three Michigan lakes crayfish stood at 46–213 kg/ha and produced 60–142 kg/ha/yr
claims.note: The abstract (Crossref) gives these spans for O. virilis biomass and annual production; the article's tables, years and methods were not seen. The paper already flags it 'abstract via a search summary': it can now say 'abstract'.

claims.claim: O. virilis 46–213 kg/ha, 60–142 kg/ha a year, P/B 0.94–1.53 (Momot & Gowing 1977)
claims.note: The abstract gives the turnover ratio 'only between 0.94 and 1.53'. Unchecked against the article. The stand-in RR1832 (Table 10, printed p. 27, PDF p. 28) gives two of the lakes year by year, 1966–73: West Lost B 51.7–142.9 kg/ha, P 56.6–133.8 kg/ha, P/B 0.94–1.38; North Twin B 33.0–82.4, P 33.6–84.6, P/B 0.85–1.39 (1970–73 under an experimental fishery). Its spans differ from the article's, so the article's 213 kg/ha must come from other years or the third lake.

claims.claim: crayfish trapped out to ~9 m in Michigan lakes (Momot & Gowing 1977)
claims.note: Not checkable in the article. The stand-in Momot & Gowing 1970 (RR1767, p. 3) supports it: traps were set in five depth bands, the deepest 'six at 9.1 m (range: 8.4–9.9 m)'; adult females were 'negligible at 9.1 m' in early summer and moved deeper by midsummer (pp. 5–6). Cite RR1767 for the depth.

notes: STAND-INS (read in full, Michigan DNR's own copies). (1) Momot & Gowing 1970, RR1767, 'Differential seasonal migration of the crayfish Orconectes virilis (Hagen), in marl lakes' — the three lakes (North Twin, South Twin, West Lost; Pigeon River area, Otsego County) are 1.5–1.9 ha limestone sink lakes with mean depths of 7.3–8.5 m, sand shoals to 3 m, peat beyond, logs in the littoral and very little vegetation (p. 4); supports the ~9-m trapping depth. (2) Momot & Gowing 1976, RR1832, 'Ricker equilibrium yield for unexploited populations of crayfish' — West Lost and North Twin (1.4 and 1.9 ha; maximum depth 13.1 and 12.5 m; alkalinity 134 ppm in West Lost; Table 1, printed p. 5, PDF p. 6), mark-recapture population estimates and Ricker production 1966–73 (Table 10, printed p. 27, PDF p. 28, read on the page image); pre-exploitation (1966–70) production averaged 101.6 kg/ha in West Lost and 64.6 kg/ha in North Twin (printed p. 26, PDF p. 27). Both are hard-water marl lakes, far from Hot Brook's soft water: the paper's own caveat ('In Maine's soft-water lakes, however, the link appears weak') matters. The 1977 article remains the right citation for the three-lake spans once read; a library copy is needed.
